subtype: Approach: one member doing everything alone [Pitfall]
passage: Class teacher's note, Wednesday. The science project group has been slow all week, and Jomon was clearly annoyed. On Tuesday night Jomon decided to finish it alone. This morning the poster arrived beautifully done, with neat writing and a working model. But Jomon's eyes were red, and Jomon yawned through the first two periods. Shreya and the other two stood at the back of the room and did not speak, and one of them said quietly that nobody had asked them. The work is good, but the group did not do it together. I will speak with each child about how to share the load.

qa.q: What did Jomon decide to do on Tuesday night?
qa.a: Jomon decided to finish the project alone.

qa.q: How might Shreya and the others be feeling at the back of the room?
qa.a: They are probably left out and hurt, since they stood silent and one said nobody had asked them.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Jomon try next time, and why?
qa.a: Jomon could tell the group what is late and ask each person to take a job with a day to finish it. That way the work is shared and nobody is tired or left out.

qa.q: How does the project look to the teacher?
qa.a: The teacher sees good work but a group that did not work together, and notices tiredness in Jomon as well as the left-out feelings.

grounding: Annoyed by delays, a member finishes the project alone at night, and the result looks good but Jomon is exhausted and the others feel left out.

subtype: Approach: one member doing everything alone [Pitfall]
passage:
Tuesday, 1:10 am
I just finished the whole model of the solar-powered house. Alone. Tanvir and the others kept saying 'tomorrow, tomorrow', and I was so fed up I decided to do it myself. Started at eight. Cut the cardboard, glued the roof, painted the panels. Mummy came in at eleven and said, 'Abhinav beta, sleep,' but I kept going. It looks really good.
Tuesday evening
I fell asleep in maths. Tanvir looked hurt when he saw the model and said, 'You didn't even call us.' The others didn't talk to me at lunch. Ma'am asked who made what. I said me. She frowned and said group work means the group.

qa.q: When did Abhinav finish the model?
qa.a: Abhinav finished it at 1:10 am, alone.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel before deciding to do it alone?
qa.a: Abhinav was fed up and annoyed with the group's 'tomorrow, tomorrow'.

qa.q: What could Abhinav have done instead of working through the night?
qa.a: Tell the group he was worried about time and set a deadline, or ask the teacher for help; doing it alone left him exhausted and the others shut out.

qa.q: How does Tanvir see the finished model?
qa.a: Tanvir looks hurt and says 'You didn't even call us', so he feels left out of his own group's project.

grounding: Shows a boy, annoyed by delays, finishing the group project alone at night, ending up exhausted while the others feel left out and the teacher notices.

subtype: Approach: one member doing everything alone [Pitfall]
passage: The group project on the village pond was due Monday, and Wasim was tired of waiting. Sachin kept going off to the fields; the others hadn't even collected leaves. On Saturday night, by the light of the kerosene lamp, Wasim did everything himself: the map of the pond, the list of birds, the drawing of the lotus, the neat heading. He went to bed after the roosters had started. On Monday the chart was the best in the class. But Wasim was yawning in the prayer line, and Sachin, looking at the chart, said, 'So we're not needed.' Masterji asked the group to explain the birds list. Only Wasim could. Masterji looked at the others for a long moment.

qa.q: What was the group project about?
How might Wasim have felt yawning in the prayer line?
qa.a: He was exhausted from working till the roosters started, and probably still resentful that the others hadn't helped.

qa.q: What would have been a better way for Wasim to handle the delays?
qa.a: Split the jobs and give each person a day to finish, or ask Masterji for help; doing everything alone cost him sleep and cut out the group.

qa.q: How does Sachin feel when he sees the chart?
qa.a: Sachin says 'So we're not needed', which suggests he felt left out and a little hurt.

grounding: Illustrates a boy who, fed up with delays, does the whole group project alone at night, leaving him exhausted and the others left out.
